Subject: Billing model review for batch rerank / per-item scoring clarification

Hi Jamie, Nathan —

Great to meet yesterday. Per follow-up, you asked for an explicit rate card and a short note on how we bill "scoring" for the batch rerank/classifier path so your finance team can model the unit economics. To keep things actionable, a few concrete asks from our side:

- Confirm the expected monthly raw query volume and the average candidate set size per query (you mentioned ~50M queries / month and ~25 candidates/query last call).
- Do you need per-query latency SLAs or is throughput/weekly backlog more important for the first rollout?
- Any required commitment horizon (monthly vs 12-month) to qualify for committed discounts?

High level — our hosted rerank/classifier endpoints can be billed two ways depending on the integration:
1) Per-scored-item: each candidate that passes through the model (common for re-rank pipelines where you score N candidates).
2) Per-call (bundle): a single bundled charge that covers up to M candidates per call (useful for small N or when caching reduces effective unit work).

I'll attach a draft rate card and a worked example based on the 50M x 25 candidate scenario so you can see the delta between per-item and bundle models. If you can confirm the volumes and any mandatory procurement dates, we'll run a quick tiered discount simulation and send a formal proposal.

Thanks —
Logan
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Thanks Logan —

Quick answers:
- Volume: our current estimate for Q4 is 50,000,000 user queries / month. That's our conservative forecast; peak could be ~70M.
- Candidate set: 20–30 candidates per query; baseline plan uses 25.
- SLA: latency is nice-to-have but not strict for v1 — throughput and predictable monthly cost matter more.
- Commitment: we prefer a 12-month committed spend if the unit economics make sense.

Can you include in the simulation:
- Tiered discounts at 10M/30M/60M monthly thresholds
- A blended cost for an integration using caching that reduces effective scored items by ~30%
- One-off eval credits for a 4-week POC (we typically need ~2M scored items worth of test traffic)

Nathan — I looped you for the technical question about bundling: if Redwood offers a per-call bundle that covers up to 50 candidates, do we still get charged extra for KV-cache misses/longer contexts?

Best,
Jamie
Head of Data Products, ShopLytics

Logan / Marissa —

Looping in a quick pricing sketch before I put a formal proposal together. Notes below; I'll attach the CSV math.

--- Pricing sketch (hosted rerank/classifier) ---
Assumptions from Jamie: 50M queries/mo, avg 25 candidates/query => 1.25B scored items/mo.
Base list price (per-scored-item): $0.000045 per scored item => $56,250/mo at list.
Per-call bundle option: $0.005 per call up to 50 candidates => 50M calls * $0.005 = $250,000/mo at list (so per-call is worse for this shape, but better when N small).
Committed discount tiers (example):
- 10% off at 10M scored items/mo
- 20% off at 30M
- 30% off at 60M

Caching adjustment example: if effective scored items reduced by 30% (due to prefix/KV reuse), scored-item bill drops to ~875M scored items => $39,375/mo at list.
POC eval credits: we can offer 2M scored-items credit for POC (internal approval required) — I tagged this PRQ-005 for Marissa to sign off.

Questions:
- Should we propose an explicit hybrid: scored-item for bulk, with an enterprise bundle SKU for low-latency single-call burst traffic?
- Can we offer a small one-time implementation credit to cover integration testing?

Ben
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: example-volume-math.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing model review for batch rerank / per-item scoring clarification

Thanks Ben — good starter numbers. A couple of internal decisions before we send a formal quote:

1) Discounting posture: for initial offer, target a blended 22% discount on list if they commit 12 months and sign to 60M+ scored items equivalent (accounting for caching). Provide a tiered fallback (15% at 30M, 10% at 10M).
2) Bundle SKU: agree to propose a hybrid path — default to per-scored-item pricing for modeling, and include an enterprise bundle option priced so it only becomes attractive for workloads with <5 candidates on avg.
3) POC credits: approve 2M scored-item credit; record as conditional on SOW and one signed PDF PO.

Logan — please confirm the commit language (monthly vs annualized committed spend) and include a clause that we reserve the right to re-evaluate kernels/quantization improvements after 6 months that could change unit cost (we want to be transparent about potential material changes).

Marissa
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Logan / Marissa / Ben —

Appreciate the quick sketch — that helps a lot. A few items from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement wants the committed spend expressed as an annual committed dollar value rather than an item count; can you provide both the item-based tiers and the equivalent annual committed spend at our expected profile (50M q/mo, 25 candidates, 30% caching)?
- Engineering wants a clear statement that per-scored-item billing excludes internal prefix cache hits and downstream deduplication (they only want to pay for actual model invocations). Please put explicit language in the SOW line item.
- POC: we'll accept the 2M scored-items credit if we can start the POC within 30 days of signing the MSA.

If you can send a short one-page proposal with the hybrid path, the two billing examples (per-item and per-call) with the annualized committed spend, and the SOW sentence around cache misses, we'll circulate internally and try to get a PO within two weeks.

Thanks —
Jamie
Head of Data Products, ShopLytics
